claims.claim: MINT AUTHORIZATION IS NEVER VERIFIED. ValidateMint checks exactly four things and none is authorization: value non-zero + provider non-empty (RejectedMalformed), mint id not already present (AlreadyApplied), FundingPool+FundingFresh == Value (RejectedConservation), FundingPool <= _poolCredits (RejectedConservation). It never reads MintBody.WitnessCert, MintBody.Envelope, or MintBody.MultiplierApplied.

The mint path has no other verification hook: Admit() does `Validate(envelope.Body)` -> Append -> Project, and Validate dispatches MintBody straight to ValidateMint. There is no cert/signature step anywhere between the caller and the WAL append.

AUTHORIZATION IS VERIFIED ONLY ON THE SPEND PATH. SpendGate calls `_certVerifier.Verify(cert, _quorum.WitnessCount)` and aborts the spend when the cert does not check out. Within my sources this is the ONLY call site that verifies a WitnessCert. (Search vocabulary over Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/, Olamnit.Coin.Rewards/, Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger/: 'WitnessCert', 'Witness', 'certVerifier', 'Verify', 'Ed25519', 'Signature'.)

SHIPPED PROOF (not a test): GenesisGrantIssuer mints a value-creating op with a WitnessCert carrying `Array.Empty<byte[]>()` signers AND `Array.Empty<byte[]>()` signatures, and the engine returns Applied. A cert with zero signers is accepted by the mint path.

TEST PROOF: the processor's own test helper builds every MintBody with `Cert(...) = new(subject, SchemeEd25519SetV1, new List<byte[]>(), new List<byte[]>())` — empty signer and signature lists — and the happy-path test asserts OpAdmission.Applied. The shipped suite therefore encodes 'a mint with no signatures is admitted' as expected behaviour.

RewardMinter's cert content is unvalidated key material: PadKey() SHA-256s any endorser key id that is not 64 hex chars, producing a 32-byte value that is NOT an Ed25519 public key, and SafeHex() returns Array.Empty<byte>() for a non-hex signature. Both are handed to the engine as a WitnessCert and the mint still applies, because ValidateMint never inspects it.

MintEnvelopeRef (QtyUCoin/WorkClass/ProofRef/Epoch) is carried but never checked: RewardMinter and GenesisGrantIssuer both pass the mint id bytes themselves as ProofRef, and ValidateMint reads no Envelope field. 'ProofRef' proves nothing on any shipped path.

The ONLY pre-mint authorization gate that exists is ROW EXISTENCE, not evidence validity: RewardMinter refuses (returns null) when no reward_endorsement row exists for the claim ('endorsed state without a row - refuse, never self-mint'). It selects endorser_key_id + signature and uses them as cert material without verifying the signature.

No signature is verified at endorsement-recording time either: RewardClaimProcessor.EndorseAsync accepts `signatureHex` as an opaque string parameter and INSERTs it into reward_endorsement, then flips the claim to `endorsed`. There is no Ed25519 verify, no length check, no hex check in this method.

The manual path is the same: ReviewQueue.EndorseAsync gates ONLY on `IsDesignated(reviewerKeyId)` — an Ordinal string equality against a configured key-id string — and then forwards the caller-supplied signatureHex unverified. Possession of the designated KEY is never demonstrated; knowing its id string is sufficient at this seam.

THE CONSERVATION AUDIT CANNOT DETECT A FORGED MINT. PoolAudit's identity is `circulating + pool == fresh` where fresh = sum(MintBody.FundingFreshUCoin) and circulating = replay TotalCirculating(). A forged fresh-funded mint of V adds V to `fresh` at PoolAudit.cs:46-47 AND creates a live DAG root of V (Project, CommutativeOpProcessor.cs:284-288) adding V to `circulating`. Both sides move by V; the identity STILL HOLDS and audit.Holds stays true. I constructed this counterexample against the code rather than accepting 'by construction'.

What PoolAudit ACTUALLY catches is exactly two defect classes: (1) POOL OVERDRAW — sum of MintBody.FundingPoolUCoin exceeds sum of AgingBody.DecayedDeltaUCoin (returns Holds=false, 'pool overdrawn'); (2) an INTRA-DAG conservation break surfaced by VerifyAllConservation(). It catches NO defect in mint authorization, endorsement, provenance, identity, or rate policy.

The shipped forgery test confirms the boundary rather than closing it: PoolAuditTests's only forged-WAL case ('PoolOverdraw_FailsTheAudit_WhenForgedIntoTheWal') forges a mint funded 500 from POOL / 0 fresh. There is no test in my sources that forges a FRESH-funded mint into the WAL — the case that passes the audit. (Vocabulary searched in Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger/: 'forge', 'forged', 'Mallory', 'bypass', 'Append(', 'Holds'.)

CoinDag.VerifyConservation is INTRA-DAG only: `live + decayed + spent == MintedValue`, where MintedValue is taken from the mint op that created the DAG (CoinDag ctor). A forged mint's DAG therefore satisfies it trivially at creation (root live == MintedValue). The DAG invariant is arithmetic self-consistency, not legitimacy of the root value.

DOC-VS-CODE DIVERGENCE (quoting a code comment): PoolAudit's summary says the pool's outflow is 'reward funding witnessed inside mint ops'. The word 'witnessed' is not backed by code — no shipped path verifies a mint's WitnessCert, so the audit sums a funding field that is asserted by the op author, not witnessed.

claims.claim: COMMENT AND CODE AGREE HERE (reported for symmetry): Project() clamps a forged pool overdraw to MicroCoin.Zero instead of throwing, and its comment says 'the pool audit is what convicts it'. PoolAudit.cs:55-58 does convict that specific case. This is the one defect class where the mint-side comment's claim is honoured by code.

Rehydration replays every WAL op through Project() WITHOUT re-running admission — so even the four ValidateMint checks are skipped on restart. The code's own comment concedes this ('rehydration Projects every WAL op WITHOUT re-running admission checks / witness-cert verification') and defers it to a cross-host follow-up. Comment and code AGREE; the gap is real and acknowledged.

SPLIT OF THE SMALLEST DENOMINATION IS REFUSED. ValidateSplit requires b.K >= 2 and b.Children.Count == b.K (else RejectedMalformed), then requires parentValue.TryFloorSplit(K) to succeed; TryFloorSplit returns false when `UCoin < k`. A 1-microcoin leaf therefore cannot split for any legal k>=2 — refused as RejectedConservation. The floor is structural, in MicroCoin, not a policy knob.

MERGE OF SMALLEST-DENOMINATION UNITS IS PERMITTED, under four conditions: >=2 parents; parents pairwise distinct; every parent a LIVE leaf; and Merged.ValueUCoin == the exact sum. Violations map to RejectedMalformed / RejectedUnknownRef / RejectedConservation respectively. Merging N 1-microcoin leaves of one mint is admissible.

MERGE ACROSS DISTINCT MINT DAGs IS REFUSED as RejectedMalformed ('v1: merge within one mint's DAG (per-coin lineage)'). Split cannot cross a DAG by construction (one ParentRef). Consequence for any batch/epoch minting design: reward units minted under DIFFERENT mint ids can never be consolidated into one leaf — holdings fragment permanently per mint.

The same one-mint-DAG restriction binds the SPEND leg twice: BalanceValidator refuses 'spend leg crosses mint DAGs - one mint per leg', and ValidateSpendProjection refuses RejectedMalformed. PaymentPlanner works around it by emitting one leg (and one commit id, and one E3PC witness round) PER MINT DAG. Per-mint fragmentation therefore scales the number of witnessed spend rounds.
Split and merge are BOTH additionally refused (RejectedReserved) when a parent leaf is reserved by an in-flight gated spend, via the reservation callback the SpendGate attaches at construction.

AUTO-ENDORSEMENT REQUIRES EXACTLY FOUR THINGS OF EVIDENCE, none cryptographic: (1) claim.EndorsementMode == 'auto'; (2) a reward_signal row loads; (3) a registered ICorroborationSource whose SourceKind string-matches signal.SourceKind; (4) that source returns a NON-NULL string. Any non-null string is accepted as `evidence_ref` — the return value's content is never inspected. Then the verifier signs and endorses.

NO SHIPPED CORROBORATOR VERIFIES A SIGNATURE. Both ICorroborationSource implementations in my sources — CoQueryCorroborationSource and IcWorkFeedCorroborationSource — do exactly the same two things: a CaptureMethod string equality ('co_event' / 'ic_work') and a set-membership test `live.Contains(signal.SourceNativeId)`, returning an interpolated string. Neither touches Ed25519Signer, a key, a digest, or signal.PayloadDigest. ABSENCE SCOPED to Olamnit.Coin.Rewards/, Olamnit.Coin/Ledger/, Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger/; vocabulary searched: 'ICorroborationSource', 'CorroborationSource', 'CorroborateAsync', 'Ed25519', 'Verify', 'Signature', 'PublicKey'.

Corroboration strength reduces to the trustworthiness of an injected delegate: both corroborators take `Func<CancellationToken, Task<IReadOnlySet<string>>> liveNativeIds` in their constructor. Nothing in my sources CONSTRUCTS either corroborator (grep for 'CorroborationSource' outside IndependentVerifier.cs hits only a prose comment in RewardsOptions.cs:70), so what actually populates that set is not established here.

claims.claim: Two of the three seeded work classes are AutoEndorsable=true ('stage-complete-co'/co_event at 1,000,000 microcoin and 'kernel-work-typed'/ic_work at 250,000); only 'kernel-work-trace'/trace_scrape is manual. So the default deployment mints on the auto path, i.e. on the unverified-signature path, for the highest-value class.

THE INDEPENDENCE CHECK CONSULTS NO BINDINGS. RewardClaimProcessor.EndorseAsync's independence rule is `string.Equals(endorserKeyId, claim.WalletId, StringComparison.Ordinal)`. The `_bindings` (ActorWalletBindingRegistry) field is used ONLY in DeriveClaimAsync (:87) and ResolveParkedAsync (:110); EndorseAsync never calls ResolveAsync. The check does not resolve the endorser through anything.

DOC-VS-CODE DIVERGENCE (quoting a doc comment): the RewardClaimProcessor class summary says 'endorsements are rejected when the endorser resolves to the claimant's own binding (US3 AS-4, SC-004)'. The code performs no resolution — it compares the endorser's KEY ID to the claim's WALLET ID as raw strings. 'resolves to the claimant's own binding' describes a mechanism that is not implemented.

claims.claim: M-36, BOTH HALVES CHECKED — the independence equality CAN fire on the auto path; it is NOT structurally impossible. Half 1: the endorser key id is a 64-char lowercase hex Ed25519 public key derived under domain separation 'olamnit-rewards-verifier-v1:' (EndorserKey.cs:22-30). Half 2: claim.WalletId is an ARBITRARY caller-supplied string — RewardsService's `bind` admin op passes `Str(root,"wallet_id")` straight into ActorWalletBindingRegistry.BindAsync, which INSERTs it with no format, length, or namespace validation. An admin who binds wallet_id to the verifier's hex public key makes the Ordinal equality true and the auto endorsement refused. Domain separation constrains only half 1.

The security consequence of the key-id-vs-wallet-id comparison runs the OTHER way too: because the two operands live in different namespaces, the check does NOT refuse an endorsement from an endorser key that is merely CONTROLLED BY the claimant but whose id differs from the wallet id string. Self-attestation is blocked only in the literal case wallet_id == endorser_key_id.

ProvenanceAudit reproduces the SAME string-equality independence check (`string.Equals(mint.endorser_key_id, mint.wallet_id, StringComparison.Ordinal)`), so the post-hoc audit inherits the identical blind spot — it is not a second, independent formulation.

ProvenanceAudit IS the only shipped code in my sources that verifies an endorsement's Ed25519 signature (over `claim_id || payload_digest || issuance_ucoin`), and it refuses non-64-hex key ids outright. But it is POST-HOC and OFF the mint path: nothing in RewardMinter, RewardsIngestionLoop, RewardsService, or CommutativeOpProcessor calls AuditAsync. A mint is never blocked by it.

ProvenanceAudit IS DRIVEN FROM THE PROVENANCE TABLE, NOT THE LEDGER — the one direction that cannot catch forgery. AuditAsync(claimId) queries reward_mint and returns NULL (not a failure) when no row exists, then checks engine-holds-mint (provenance -> ledger). There is no ledger -> provenance direction and no enumeration API: a mint appended straight to the WAL with no reward_mint row produces no report at all and is invisible to this audit.

DOC-VS-CODE DIVERGENCE (quoting a doc comment): ProvenanceAudit's summary asserts '100% of minted rewards must verify (SC-004); any break returns a named failure, never a silent pass.' The code can only speak about rewards that HAVE a reward_mint row; for a WAL mint with no provenance row it returns null — which is neither a verify nor a named failure. The '100% of minted rewards' scope the comment claims is not the scope the code covers.
